correctness.rationale: For every \(m\ge2\) with strict fixed rankings and a shared uniform permutation, the clock-transposition identity isolates the difference of two record indicators. Conditional integration over t<s and the elements with intermediate p ranks telescopes exactly to \(1/[r(r+1)]\), with \(r\ge1\). Adjacent-inversion paths prove unique extremizers and independent initial ranks prove exact harmonic endpoints. An extracted exact-rational verifier checked 152 direct enumerations, 872 pair moments and 2283 adjacent swaps. Finite checks supplement but do not prove the general theorem.

originality.rationale: The exact strict adjacent-preference-swap decrement under one uniformly shared display order is not implied by the 2026 anchor-proofness theorem, by the classical joint lower/upper record endpoint literature, or by positive association results for permutation up-set events. Several targeted indexed-literature queries did not recover the same quantified statement; priority risk from unindexed record-covariance studies remains. A failed search alone was not treated as proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Shared presentation is a natural user-interface constraint in sequential candidate evaluation. The exact finite-m sensitivity detects strict loss of joint information as two preferences disagree, classifies best/worst covariance uniquely, and shows reversal produces negative covariance despite common randomization. This nontrivial local-to-global law gives structural information beyond record-count marginals and is a plausible base for quantifying effects of random shared candidate displays. The model assumptions sharply delimit the interpretation.
